title: The base change morphism on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\neq\ell$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). For each such scheme $T$, write $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)$ for the bounded constructible derived category of module objects on $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ over the coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_T$ pulled back from $\Lambda$ on the point ([sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]). Assume that the derived pushforwards carry bounded constructible complexes to bounded constructible complexes, so they restrict as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors]. This hypothesis holds, for example, for $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E,\underline E$ with $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $\cO_E$ its ring of integers, and for $\Lambda=\underline{\Qlb}$ with $\Qlb$ the fixed algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ endowed with its specified condensed-ring structure ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]).
Fix a commutative square of schemes and morphisms of the setting

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{\;g'\;} & X\\
{\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\
Y' & \xrightarrow{\;g\;} & Y
\end{array}
\qquad f\circ g'=g\circ f'.
$$

All functors below are the restricted functors on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(-,\Lambda)$ of
[sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors].

The *pullback comparison* of the square is the natural isomorphism

$$
\theta_{sq}\colon Lf'^*\circ Lg^*\cong L(g\circ f')^*=L(f\circ g')^*\cong Lg'^*\circ Lf^*,
$$

built from the two composition isomorphisms and the commutativity of the square.

The *base change morphism* $\mathrm{BC}_{sq}\colon Lg^*\circ Rf_*\to Rf'_*\circ Lg'^*$ of functors
$D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y',\Lambda)$ is the composite of three steps:

$$
Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\ \eta'\ }Rf'_*Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow[\ \sim\ ]{\ \theta_{sq}\ }Rf'_*Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }Rf'_*Lg'^*.
$$

The first step inserts the unit $\eta'$ of $Lf'^*\dashv Rf'_*$. The second transports along
$\theta_{sq}$. The third contracts the counit $\varepsilon$ of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. No hypothesis on
the square (such as being cartesian) or on $\Lambda$ beyond the above enters the definition.

proof.text: The standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] supplies the schemes, morphisms, coefficient sheaf and categories $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(-,\Lambda)$. Under the stated preservation hypothesis, [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors] supplies the restricted functors $Lf^*$ and $Rf_*$ for every arrow in the square and the restricted adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. Thus all functors and adjunction units and counits appearing below are defined on the stated bounded constructible categories.

Apply [det-def-sfb-base-change-morphism-comparison] to the displayed square with the same prime $\ell$, field $k$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes, four $k$-morphisms and commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$. Its statement requires only commutativity, and supplies $c_{f',g}:L(g\circ f')^*\cong Lf'^*Lg^*$ and $c_{g',f}:L(f\circ g')^*\cong Lg'^*Lf^*$. With $e:L(g\circ f')^*\cong L(f\circ g')^*$ the equality-induced isomorphism, its formula is $\theta_{sq}=c_{g',f}\circ e\circ c_{f',g}^{-1}$. Both composite scheme maps go from $X'$ to $Y$, so this is a natural isomorphism of functors $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X',\Lambda)$ in exactly the direction asserted. No cartesian hypothesis or pushforward preservation is needed for this comparison.

Use [det-def-sfb-base-change-morphism-bc] with the comparison of step 2 and the assumed preservation of bounded constructible complexes by pushforward. At $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$ its specified composite starts at $Lg^*Rf_*K$, inserts $\eta'_{Lg^*Rf_*K}$ to reach $Rf'_*Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*K$, applies $Rf'_*(\theta_{sq,Rf_*K})$ to reach $Rf'_*Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*K$, and applies $Rf'_*Lg'^*(\varepsilon_K)$ to reach $Rf'_*Lg'^*K$. The cited statement supplies exactly this natural transformation, which is the unit–comparison–counit construction in the item. For a morphism $u:K\to K_1$, naturality of the unit makes the first component square commute; naturality of $\theta_{sq}$ at $Rf_*u$, followed by the functor $Rf'_*$, makes the second commute; and naturality of the counit at $u$, followed by $Rf'_*Lg'^*$, makes the third commute. Pasting these three squares proves naturality of the composite. No assertion that the square is cartesian or that this transformation is invertible is used.
